title: Minimum Consecutive Cards to Pick Up
statement: The array `cards` lists card values in a row, and two cards match when their values are equal. You may take any contiguous run of cards. Return the length of the shortest run that contains at least one matching pair, or `-1` if no two cards in the whole array match.
notes:
## Intuition

Any run that contains a matching pair can be trimmed until it starts at one card of the pair and ends at the other, so the answer is the shortest distance between two equal cards, plus one. Comparing every pair finds it in O(n²). For a fixed right end `i`, the best partner is the most recent earlier card with the same value: an older one only makes the run longer. Remembering the last index of each value in a hash map gives that partner in O(1).

## Approach

1. Keep `lastSeen`, a map from card value to the latest index where it appeared, and `best = Infinity`.
2. Walk the cards left to right with index `i`.
3. If `card` was seen before, the run from its last index to `i` holds a pair; its length is `i - lastSeen.get(card) + 1`. Keep the smaller of that and `best`.
4. Record `i` as the latest index of `card`.
5. If `best` is still `Infinity`, no value repeats, so return `-1`; otherwise return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`cards = [3, 4, 2, 3, 4, 7]`.

- `i = 0..2`: `3`, `4` and `2` are new; `lastSeen = {3: 0, 4: 1, 2: 2}`.
- `i = 3`: `3` was last at 0, so the run has length `3 - 0 + 1 = 4`; `best = 4`.
- `i = 4`: `4` was last at 1, length `4 - 1 + 1 = 4`; `best` stays `4`.
- `i = 5`: `7` is new. The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with O(1) map operations.
- Space: O(n) for the map in the worst case (all values distinct).

## Pitfalls

- The length counts both ends: it is `i - previous + 1`, not `i - previous`.
- Update the stored index on every visit, matched or not, so the next match measures from the closest copy.
- Return `-1` when nothing repeats instead of leaking `Infinity`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `lastSeen` | map from card value to its most recent index |
| `best` | shortest run with a matching pair found so far |
| `i` | index of the current card |
| `card` | value of the current card |

narration.2: Map each card value to the most recent index where it appeared.
narration.3: No matching pair has been seen yet, so the shortest run is still infinite.
narration.5: Visit each card once, from left to right.
narration.8: Then the run from its previous copy to here holds a pair; keep the shortest such run.
narration.10: Remember this index as the latest copy of the value, so later matches stay as short as possible.
narration.13: No value repeated means no pair exists, so answer -1; otherwise return the shortest run.
